questions.stem: Which splice joins two ropes without increasing the diameter, so the rope can still run through a block?
options: Short splice
Long splice
Eye splice
Back splice
questions.explanation: A long splice keeps the original diameter, so the rope still runs through a block. A short splice joins two ropes but is thicker and cannot pass through a block. An eye splice makes a loop and a back splice finishes an end.

questions.stem: What is an eye splice used for?
options: To make a permanent loop at the end of a rope
To join two ropes end to end without a knot
To shorten a rope without cutting it
To stop a rope running out through a block
questions.explanation: An eye splice makes a permanent loop at the rope's end. Joining two ropes is a short or long splice, shortening is done with a sheepshank, and stopping a rope running out is the job of a stopper knot.

questions.stem: Why is a short splice not suitable for a rope that must run through a block?
options: It is far too weak to take the load of a running line
The join ends up thicker than the rest of the rope
It can only be made in wire rope, not in fibre rope
It unlays as soon as it gets wet and must be remade
questions.explanation: The short splice is strong but the overlapping strands make the join thicker, so it can jam in the block. A long splice keeps the diameter. The short splice is not weak and is made in fibre rope.

questions.stem: You will make a short splice by unlaying 1.0 m of each rope. About how much would a long splice of the same rope need?
options: About 1.0 m
About 2.0 m
About 4.0 m
About 10 m
questions.explanation: A long splice needs rope unlaid for about four times the length of a short splice, so 4 x 1.0 m = about 4.0 m on each rope. It is the extra length that lets the strands taper and keeps the diameter the same.

questions.stem: Which list names the three-strand splices in TP 10936?
options: Short, long, cut, eye and back
Reef, bowline, clove and rolling
Common, palm-and-needle and West Country
Flat, round and racking
questions.explanation: TP 10936 lists the short, long, cut, eye and back splices for three-strand rope, plus an eight-strand eye splice and a braided eye splice. The other lists are knots, whippings and seizing types.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a whipping?
options: To stop the rope end from fraying or unlaying
To join two ropes together end to end
To give the rope a decorative loop at the end
To make the end of the rope float in the water
questions.explanation: A whipping is a tight wrap of twine that stops a rope's end fraying or unlaying. It joins nothing, and it has no effect on buoyancy.

questions.stem: A hawser's end needs a whipping that will last for years. Which is the better choice than a common whipping?
options: A palm-and-needle whipping
A reef knot tied in the end
A sheepshank near the end
Leaving the end unwhipped
questions.explanation: A palm-and-needle whipping is sewn through the strands and is a more permanent way of securing a rope end than a common whipping. A reef knot or sheepshank is not a whipping, and an unwhipped end will unlay.

questions.stem: Which description fits a cut splice?
options: A loop formed part-way along between two ropes
A join between two ropes that keeps the rope's original diameter
A finish that tucks the strands back into the rope's own end
A permanent loop made at the very end of a single rope
questions.explanation: A cut splice forms a loop between two ropes, part-way along. The second option describes a long splice, the third a back splice and the fourth an eye splice.

questions.stem: While uncoiling a wire rope for splicing, a kink forms. What is the correct view?
options: Heave the wire taut on the winch and the kink will pull out
Strain will not remove it; the wire is unsafe to work
The kink only matters if the wire gets wet, so keep it dry
Tape over the kink so it cannot snag, and carry on splicing
questions.explanation: Once a kink is made no amount of strain takes it out, and the rope is unsafe to work. Wire should be uncoiled using a turntable or by rolling it, and never lifted off in loops that kink.

questions.stem: Which of these is a recognised way of whipping a rope end, besides the common whipping?
options: West Country whipping
Sheet bend whipping
Cut-splice whipping
Eye-splice whipping
questions.explanation: West Country whipping (a symmetric whipping made with half knots on alternate sides, finished with a reef knot) and American whipping (sometimes used for hawser ends) are both recognised alternatives to the common whipping, as is the palm-and-needle whipping. The other names are not whippings.
